stories.title: Insufficient evidence to link bomb threats across Europe to foreign powers: Macron
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday there was insufficient evidence to determine whether foreign powers were behind a wave of bomb threats across Europe.
Read: EU flights hit by wave of bomb hoaxes "We are obviously very vigilant in the face of this epidemic of bomb alerts and threats," Macron said.
Italy also faced a wave of bomb threats targeting schools on Wednesday, prompting evacuations and security checks.

stories.title: UAE says 14 killed, 30 injured in Fujairah traffic accident
summary: At least 14 people were killed and 30 others injured in a pileup involving 18 vehicles and five trucks in Fujairah, an emirate in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the UAE Ministry of Interior said Thursday.
The ministry added in a post ​on ​X ⁠that emergency and ​specialised teams ​were ⁠continuing to deal with the ⁠aftermath ​of ​the accident.

Ministry of Interior: Authorities Continue Efforts to Address Fujairah Traffic Accident The Ministry of Interior has reported a major multi-vehicle crash in the Emirate of Fujairah involving 18 cars and trucks.

stories.title: Netflix faces backlash for keeping Russell Brand’s comedy special after conviction
summary: Netflix is facing criticism for keeping Russell Brand’s stand-up special, Russell Brand: Re, in its catalogue following the comedian’s conviction for rape and sexual assault.
Netflix classifies the special as TV-MA.
Others questioned whether Brand continues to receive payments from the special, while some criticised Netflix’s decision to keep it available.

stories.title: Poisonous substance detected in sample after 5 children die in Khyber
summary: Laboratory tests confirmed the presence of a poisonous substance in a sample taken from one of five children who died after a suspected poisoning incident in the Bazaar Zakha Khel area of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Khyber district, officials said on Thursday.
At least seven children were affected by the suspected poisonous substance, five of whom died while two others fell unconscious.
Reports received from Khyber Medical College confirmed the presence of poisonous material in a sample taken from one of the children.

stories.title: ECP strikes MQM-P's Khalid Maqbool off party leadership list
summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has removed Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui’s name as the convener of Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) from its official website, leaving the party among 13 political parties without a recognised head in the commission's records.
Meanwhile, the ECP has issued a show-cause notice to MQM-P over its failure to hold intra-party elections.

The removal of Siddiqui's name from the ECP website comes amid the party’s failure to hold fresh intra-party elections within the prescribed timeframe, raising questions about its leadership status in the commission's official records.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral visuals do not show violence in Balochistan; they are unrelated and old
summary: How it started On Nov 10, a pro-PTI account, based on its past posts, shared a video on X allegedly showing a mosque in Balochistan, destroyed with bullet holes and heavy firearms.

A pro-Afghan account later shared the same video with the following caption: “Armed men set several fully loaded trucks on fire near Turbat.” The video was also shared by other smaller accounts here, here, here and here.

A reverse image search was conducted to trace the source of the viral video and yielded a clip shared on Facebook on September 21, 2026, by a Nigerian with the following caption: “This is Malam Fatori.

stories.title: Russell Brand’s Instagram and Facebook accounts disabled by Meta after sentencing
summary: Russell Brand’s social media accounts on platforms owned by Meta have been disabled following his conviction for rape and sexual assault.
Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, has disabled Brand’s accounts.
Meta’s community standards policy states that, “in order to maintain a safe environment and empower free expression”, the company restricts or removes accounts considered “harmful to the community”.

stories.title: Barrister Gohar visits Qureshi in hospital after jail fall
summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan visited the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) on Thursday to enquire about the health of party leader Shah Mahmood Qureshi, who remains in the hospital for treatment.

Also Read: ATC extends Qureshi's bail in several cases Meanwhile, Imran Khan’s sisters Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were released from Kot Lakhpat jail today, where they had been held since September 21 under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance.
Imran was also taken from Adiala jail to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences overnight on November 10 and 11 for eye treatment, and met his lawyers at the jail on Wednesday.

stories.title: One killed, four wounded in Washington DC shooting, police say
summary: One person was killed, and four others ‌were shot and wounded when a gunman opened fire inside a gym before barricading himself inside an apartment building in Washington DC on Thursday morning, police said.
BREAKING: The suspect believed to be behind this morning’s deadly shooting in Washington, D.C., has shot himself after spending more than an hour talking with police negotiators.
Police were clearing a nearby apartment building when gunshots rang out on ‌the ⁠seventh floor where the suspect had barricaded himself, Carroll said.

stories.title: Who is Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress?
summary: Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress is set to take over as interim CEO from Jensen Huang, the company said on Thursday, putting her in charge of the chipmaker whose processors ​power the world's most advanced supercomputers and AI data centres.

CFO since 2013 Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 ​as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. ​She has appeared alongside Jensen Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls.
Career before ​Nvidia Before Nvidia, Kress spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments, then worked at Microsoft ​from 1997 to 2010.

stories.title: Türkiye, Saudi Arabia ready to deepen defence ties and expand joint production
summary: Türkiye was ready to expand defence industry cooperation with Saudi Arabia, backed by over 1,400 projects and a $120 billion portfolio, the country's top defence official said on Thursday.
He also noted that the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (Tubitak) provided 65 billion liras in support to over 2,200 defence projects and more than 4,000 researchers.
Gul noted that SAHA Istanbul had elevated defence industry clustering, transferring Türkiye's accumulated expertise to both domestic organisations and international stakeholders.

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down in big blow to AI boom
summary: Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter ​said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive ⁠who reported to him.
Read: Could Nvidia lose longtime CEO Jensen Huang amid growing controversy?
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raised national security concerns.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral visuals of Imran Khan meeting his lawyers in Adiala jail are AI-generated
summary: Several people, mostly PTI supporters, shared visuals across social media platforms X and Facebook on November 11, 2026, allegedly showing PTI founder Imran Khan meeting with his lawyers in Adiala jail.
How it started On Nov 11, a pro-PTI account shared an image on X, allegedly showing Imran sitting and talking with his lawyers, Salman Safdar and Sardar Latif Khosa, inside a room in Adiala jail.
Fact-check status: False The claim that viral visuals show Imran Khan meeting his lawyers inside Adiala jail on November 11, 2026, is false.

stories.title: Turkiye says Makkah pact has strengthened solidarity with Pakistan as PM Shehbaz meets Erdogan
summary: Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif held a bilateral meeting with President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan of Türkiye today on the sidelines of UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) COP31 Leaders Summit.

In a post on X, the prime minister said, “We agreed to build a forward-looking Pakistan-Finland partnership in trade, technology, education and climate resilience.” Pleased to meet President @alexstubb on the sidelines of #COP31 in Antalya.

PM Shehbaz reaffirms solidarity with Sudan The prime minister met Sudan's Transitional Sovereignty Council President General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Sudan’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity.

stories.title: Russell Brand documentary announced by Netflix days after prison sentence
summary: Netflix has announced Russell Brand: Open Secret, a documentary examining the comedian and actor’s rise to fame, the allegations that emerged in 2023 and the criminal trial that ended with his conviction.
The allegations against Brand first became public in 2023 through reporting by The Sunday Times and a Channel 4 Dispatches programme.
The Metropolitan Police has confirmed that Brand remains under investigation over further rape allegations made by two other women.

stories.title: Jensen Huang hit with fresh controversy as alleged new affair with Nvidia VP emerges
summary: Jensen Huang is facing fresh scrutiny after reports emerged alleging that the Nvidia chief executive had a relationship with another senior figure at the company, adding to the controversy surrounding his personal life.
Huang co founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company through its rise to become one of the world’s most influential technology businesses.
Nvidia’s board investigation and the reported discussions about Huang’s future have placed the chief executive under growing scrutiny as the company faces questions about its leadership.

stories.title: Police confirm helping Jemima Goldsmith remove Russell Brand from her home amid 2014 abuse claim
summary: Thames Valley Police have confirmed that officers helped Jemima Goldsmith remove former boyfriend Russell Brand from her Oxfordshire home in July 2014 following an alleged violent incident.
Goldsmith, who dated Brand for approximately a year around 2014, disclosed the incident in a social media statement on Monday.
Goldsmith had reportedly asked Brand to leave and that officers communicated her request to him before he agreed to leave the property.

stories.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after US midterms losses
summary: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, US President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of foreign policy on the global stage.

With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington.
High-profile meeting Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Cummins to address Khawaja 'Sandpapergate' claims
summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins said he plans to address Usman Khawaja's "long list of allegations" about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal on Friday after taking time to "better understand" them.

In the book, Khawaja alleges that the whole team, including Cummins, knew about the plot to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing during the third Test against South Africa at Cape Town eight years ago.
Former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick, who was on the South Africa tour, also rubbished Khawaja's allegations, calling them "absolutely false" in an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald.

stories.title: China's Xi says Taiwan 'reunification' must happen as history cannot be stopped
summary: Resolving the Taiwan question is an "unwavering historical mission" of China's Communist Party, Xi said in a speech in Beijing's Great Hall of the People.

Beijing calls Sun a great national hero and patriot, as well as the forerunner of the 1949 communist ​revolution that forced the defeated Republic of ​China government to flee to Taiwan, ⁠where it remains to this day.

Taiwan has ⁠been particularly upset ​by Beijing's effort to claim credit for the victory in World War Two, saying it was the ​Republic of China government that fought alongside the allies, as the People's Republic of China did not exist at the time.

stories.title: Bilawal and I 'almost' on same page over 'system reset': Naqvi
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday said he and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari were almost on the same page regarding a reset of the system, while stressing that any major decision would require agreement among political parties.
Highlighting the NCCIA's operations, Naqvi said the agency had uncovered a major international "education-related fraud involving approximately 5,000 Pakistanis".
The minister also "referred to separate cases involving a call centre and a child victim, saying the agency had taken action in those matters".

stories.title: Manchester United sack manager Carrick with club in relegation zone
summary: Manchester United have dismissed manager Michael Carrick, the club said on Thursday, after a prolonged winless Premier League run culminated in a 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa last weekend, leaving the team mired in the relegation ‌zone.

United have won only three of their 15 matches in all competitions under Carrick this season -- including one league victory -- leaving them 18th in the table on eight points after 10 games, one point from the bottom.

A 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma in ⁠the Champions League briefly eased the pressure on Carrick, but United's familiar defensive frailties were exposed again in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, despite two injury-time goals salvaging a point.

stories.title: Rizwanullah powers Pakistan into ACC Asia Cup final
summary: Fast bowler Rizwanullah claimed five wickets before openers Hayam Khan and Usman Khan struck half-centuries as defending champions Pakistan stormed into the ACC Under-19 Asia Cup final with a nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh on Thursday.
Rizwanullah led Pakistan's bowling attack with figures of 5-30 from eight overs as Bangladesh were dismissed for 138 in 31.4 overs after being put under pressure by the defending champions.
Usman remained unbeaten on 64 from 54 deliveries, including seven fours and two sixes, while Abdul Qadir finished on eight not out as Pakistan completed the chase comfortably.

stories.title: US envoys go to Kremlin for talks with Putin on Ukraine
summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived at the ​Kremlin on Thursday for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in a new push for a peace deal in Ukraine despite what they have called a lack ‌of trust between Moscow and Kyiv.

The negotiations are the 10th time Witkoff has met Putin in person during a conflict that has lasted longer than the Soviet Union's fight against Nazi Germany in World War Two, and follow two days of US-led trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi.
As he entered a Moscow hotel before the ​Kremlin talks, Witkoff was asked by a reporter whether progress made in the talks so far meant peace was closer.

stories.title: Uzma Khan, Noreen Niazi released after withdrawal of MPO orders, says lawyer
summary: Sisters of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, Noreen Niazi and Dr Uzma Khan were released from jail on Thursday following the withdrawal of their detention orders under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) law, PTI lawyer Taimur Malik said.
Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi have been released upon withdrawal of their unlawful MPO detention order.
Separately, Noreen’s son, Wali, questioned the detention and release of his mother and aunt, Dr Uzma, saying they had spent 53 days in Kot Lakhpat Jail without being charged or tried.

stories.title: Australia set to unleash new bowling hope Beardman against England
summary: Australia will unleash their new pace bowling hope Mahli Beardman in the first of three one-dayers against England on Friday, with skipper Mitchell Marsh calling him "an amazing talent".
"He's an amazing talent, a ripping young kid," Marsh told reporters in confirming the 21-year-old Beardman would make his ODI debut on his home ground.
England will once more heavily rely on veteran Joe Root to anchor the batting and Jofra Archer to lead the attack.

stories.title: Pakistan ready to take 'all necessary defensive measures' to protect Saudi Arabia: DG ISPR
summary: The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz urges grant-based climate finance, warns against 'weaponising water' at COP31
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday urged grant-based financing for countries affected by climate change, while also warning against "weaponising water." "National effort cannot replace a fair and just global response when climate disaster strikes.

The prime minister said national efforts to combat climate change could not replace a fair and just global response. “When climate disasters strike, vulnerable countries need timely help and finance that does not deepen their debt,” he said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif highlights the devastating impact of climate change, with 33 million people affected by floods.

stories.title: Finance minister dubs mining sector a ‘game-changer’ for Pakistan’s economy at investment forum in Islamabad
summary: The forum brought together international investors and government officials as Pakistan sought to attract foreign investment in its mineral sector, with provincial leaders outlining investment opportunities, incentives and development plans.
He further said the Pakistan Investment Policy 2023 provided protection to investors and highlighted the government's efforts to strengthen the country's investment environment.
The chief minister also highlighted efforts to increase the value of pink salt exports, saying the mineral had previously been exported in raw form, limiting Pakistan's earnings.

stories.title: Snowfall blocks road to Babusar Top
summary: Heavy snowfall from Baiser to Babusar Top in Naran Valley has covered the surrounding mountains with a white blanket of snow and blocked the road, affecting traffic movement in the upper Kaghan Valley.

The meteorological department has forecast the first snowfall of the winter season in the country's northern mountains this week, with rain and thunderstorms expected in several regions, including the federal capital, as a new weather system moves across the country.
The forecast covers November 10-14, with snowfall expected over higher elevations in upper K-P, G-B and Kashmir.

stories.title: Faulty vehicle in President Zardari’s motorcade prompts Sindh police inquiry
summary: The inclusion of an unroadworthy vehicle in President Asif Ali Zardari’s motorcade during his Thatta visit has triggered a high-level inquiry by the Sindh police, with the IGP seeking a report within seven days.

According to a notification issued by the office of the inspector general of police (IGP) Sindh on Nov 3, 2026, a three-member committee has been formed to investigate the inclusion of the faulty vehicle in the presidential convoy.

The committee will determine how a faulty and unroadworthy vehicle was assigned duty in the president’s motorcade and identify the officers and personnel responsible for its inspection and deployment.

stories.title: Security protocol keeps PPP leaders waiting outside Zardari House for hours
summary: A visit to meet President Asif Ali Zardari turned into a test of patience for several senior Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leaders on Wednesday, as they spent more than two hours waiting outside Zardari House in Nawabshah.
Several senior PPP leaders and elected representatives visited Zardari House to meet the president but had to wait for more than two hours before being allowed inside.
The prolonged wait by senior PPP leaders and local government representatives created an unusual scene outside Zardari House.
